issue: Spelling consistency: the harmonisation pass made US "theater" the house form (and 18:99 has "Variety Theater"); the poster still has British "THEATRE".
old: VARIETY THEATRE
new: VARIETY THEATER

issue: Addition: the Russian says only that the wind blew the sheets about; "off the table" is invented.
old: They had been blown off the table by the wind
new: They had been blown about by the wind

issue: Stiff calque: «ну его в болото» is an idiom of dismissal ("to blazes with him"); "the swamp can have him" reads as a literal image an English reader stumbles on.
old: the swamp can have him!
new: to blazes with him!

issue: Addition: «дырявом» means only "full of holes"; "battered" is added and doubles the idea.
old: a battered yellow bowler with holes in it
new: a yellow bowler full of holes

issue: English grammar: the conditional does not attach to "a girl good in every way"; reads as a broken sentence.
russian: всем хорошая девица, кабы не портил ее причудливый шрам на шее
old: a girl good in every way if a bizarre scar on her neck had not spoiled her
new: a girl who would have been perfect in every way had a bizarre scar on her neck not spoiled her

issue: Pronoun consistency: the cat is "it/its" throughout this chapter (12:21, 12:80, 12:102, 12:113, 12:117); "himself" here breaks it.
russian: кот от себя добавил футлярчик с помадой
old: the cat added a little case of lipstick from himself
new: the cat added a little case of lipstick on its own account

issue: Stiff calque: "a beginning and promising actress" is not idiomatic English for «начинающей и подающей надежды актрисой».
old: a beginning and promising actress
new: a promising young actress just starting out

issue: Calque: «одному типу» is "some guy"; "some type" is not idiomatic English on its own and blurs the slangy register the master then objects to.
old: I socked some type in the mug
new: I socked some guy in the mug

issue: Shade of meaning: «Нехороший цвет» is ominous ("a bad color", an evil sign, cf. «желтому знаку» in 13:97), not aesthetic; "ugly" loses the portent.
old: An ugly color.
new: Not a good color.

issue: Ambiguity: "she saw me alone" can be read as "saw me when I was alone"; the Russian «увидела она меня одного» means she saw only him among thousands.
old: she saw me alone
new: she saw me and only me

issue: Inconsistent sound: «не стукнет ли ... калитка» is a bang/click, and the next sentence repeats it as "The gate bangs, my heart bangs" («Стукнет калитка, стукнет сердце»); "creak" breaks the echo.
old: listening for the creak of the decrepit gate
new: listening for the bang of the decrepit gate

issue: English word order: "endlessly" is stranded after the object and seems to modify "written".
old: she reread what had been written endlessly
new: she endlessly reread what had been written

issue: Wrong sense: «я боюсь» is the master saying he is frightened (the fear motif of 13:151–186); "I’m afraid" at the end of the sentence reads as the polite hedge "I regret to say", so the confession of fear is lost.
russian: я уже не в силах идти один обратно, я боюсь
old: to come back alone, I’m afraid
new: to come back alone; I am frightened

issue: Tense: «сделал бы это лучше меня» is a present conditional (Woland would tell it better); "would have done" suggests a missed past chance.
russian: А ваш знакомый с Патриарших сделал бы это лучше меня
old: would have done it better than I could
new: would do it better than I could

issue: US spelling consistency: elsewhere "mustache" (3:42, 4:35, 7:82, 18:201, 18:227).
old: A thin, moustached cabby
new: A thin, mustached cabby

issue: US spelling consistency (as above).
old: The moustached man’s face
new: The mustached man’s face

issue: Echo: this sentence deliberately points back to 13:34 («толстяка с багровой физиономией»), which the translation renders "fat man with a purple physiognomy"; the callback should use the same words.
old: the fat man with the crimson face
new: the fat man with the purple physiognomy

issue: Wrong shade: «задушевно» is "warmly, in a heart-to-heart tone" (the interrogator's false intimacy); "sincerely" asserts sincerity.
old: they asked Nikanor Ivanovich sincerely
new: they asked Nikanor Ivanovich in a heart-to-heart tone

issue: Wrong verb: «промычал» is "mumbled/moaned" (he is on his knees, cf. «мычание» in 15:23, rendered "moan"); "bellowed" is too loud.
old: he bellowed
new: he moaned

issue: Wrong shade: «задушевно» = "warmly, confidingly", as in 15:13; "sincerely" misstates the tone.
old: the young artiste said sincerely
new: the young artiste said warmly

issue: Stiff wording: «втянулась на Лысую Гору» describes the column winding its way up; "drew itself up onto" is unidiomatic and suggests standing to attention.
old: it drew itself up onto Bald Mountain
new: it wound its way up onto Bald Mountain

issue: Wrong referent: «глаза выедал ослепительный блеск» means the glare stung the onlookers’ eyes; "the eyes were eaten away" reads as if the lion masks’ eyes were eroded.
old: the eyes were eaten away by the blinding glitter
new: the blinding glitter stung the eyes

issue: English grammar/register: "had liked ... extremely" is not idiomatic, and jars in the solemn Yershalaim register.
old: who had liked Yeshua’s preaching extremely
new: who had been greatly taken with Yeshua’s preaching

issue: Stiff calque: «кинулись бежать с холма» = "rushed down the hill"; "rushed to run" is awkward.
russian: Счастливые солдаты кинулись бежать с холма
old: The happy soldiers rushed to run down the hill
new: The happy soldiers rushed down the hill

issue: Calque: «поставить на них резолюции» means writing official instructions/endorsements on papers (10:56 renders «резолюциях» as "instructions on documents"); "writing resolutions" suggests a meeting's motions.
russian: с явной целью поставить на них резолюции
old: with the evident aim of writing resolutions on them
new: with the evident aim of writing his instructions on them

issue: English grammar: the relative clause "who perhaps did not have perfect pitch" is separated from Kosarchuk by "them all".
russian: Всех повел за собою Косарчук, у которого
old: Kosarchuk led them all, who perhaps
new: They were all led by Kosarchuk, who perhaps

issue: Consistency: грузовик is "truck" everywhere else in the book (4:62, 5:102, 6:91, 13:192, 19:46…); British "lorry" appears only in 17:104–105.
old: three lorries
new: three trucks

issue: Consistency: "truck", as above.
old: the first lorry
new: the first truck

issue: Consistency: "truck", as above.
old: The second lorry
new: The second truck

issue: Consistency: "truck", as above.
old: at the lorries
new: at the trucks

issue: Glossary: домоуправление is "house management" (GLOSSARY.md, unified in HARMONISATION.md §1; cf. 15:14, 15:22).
old: the management office of building No. 302-bis
new: the house management of building No. 302-bis

issue: Broken sentence: the Russian breaks off after «чтоб их всех сразу...» ("that all of them at once..."); "why did they all have to be at once..." reads as an English grammar error rather than a trailing-off.
russian: И нужно ж было, чтоб их всех сразу...
old: And why did they all have to be at once...
new: And why did it have to be all of them at once...

issue: Idiom: «Не ушиблись ли вы?» is solicitous ("You haven’t hurt yourself, have you?"); "Haven’t you hurt yourself?" sounds as if Woland expected him to be hurt.
old: Haven’t you hurt yourself?
new: You haven’t hurt yourself, have you?
